root_causes.explanation: OrderAPI create_order now returns the order identifier under the key "id" (e.g. {"status":"created","id":"ORD-0001"}). The bot's field_mappings.order_id is still "order_id", so after the customer confirms it cannot read the order ID. It then returns a generic 'system trouble' message without calling confirm_order or charge. This matches all 6 failed chats: no errors, no 4xx/5xx, normal latency, and no confirm_order or charge calls in any trace.

resolution.report: All 6 chats that reached the confirmation step failed. The bot quoted correctly and create_order succeeded (ORD-0001 to ORD-0006), but none of them was confirmed or charged. There were no HTTP errors, no latency problems and no invariant violations. The create_order response now returns the order identifier as "id" instead of "order_id", while field_mappings.order_id still points to "order_id". The bot fails after the customer's 'yes' with a generic system-trouble message. The patch remaps order_id to "id". No charge calls were made, so no money moved without an order. The 6 orders created during the incident (ORD-0001 to ORD-0006) are unconfirmed and unpaid, and the team may want to clean them up or re-contact those customers. After the patch, verify that the next chats reach confirm_order and charge. The ar_10 chat was a genuine customer cancel and is not part of the incident.

resolution.report: Eight of ten chats failed because StockAPI returned 429 (retry-after: 1s) on check_stock, and the bot had max_retries=0, so it gave up after one attempt. The two chats that got through completed correctly: order, charge, webhook and confirm were all consistent, and there were no invariant violations or money-without-order cases. The patch sets retry.max_retries=3 and retry.backoff_s=1.0, giving waits of about 1s, 2s and 4s that respect the retry-after hint. 429 is already in retry_on. 429 means the request was rejected, so retrying is safe. If 429s persist after this change, follow up with the StockAPI owners about rate limits or request volume. Also note that stock responses report cached:true. This did not cause any visible issue here, so I changed nothing for it.
